summary_en: This Phase 2 trial tests abemaciclib, with or without hydroxychloroquine, to target disseminated tumor cells in the bone marrow of people with breast cancer. Both drugs are taken as pills twice a day; abemaciclib is 150 mg twice daily in one arm and 100 or 150 mg twice daily in the other, and the length of treatment is not stated. The main outcome is not stated in the record; the study is a Phase 2 pilot trial.
summary_es: Este ensayo de fase 2 evalúa abemaciclib, con o sin hidroxicloroquina, para atacar las células tumorales diseminadas en la médula ósea de personas con cáncer de mama. Ambos medicamentos se toman como pastillas dos veces al día; el abemaciclib es de 150 mg dos veces al día en un grupo y de 100 o 150 mg dos veces al día en el otro, y la duración del tratamiento no se indica. El resultado principal no se indica en el registro; el estudio es un ensayo piloto de fase 2.
who_for: Invasive primary breast cancer diagnosed within 5 years of entry into companion protocol UPCC 28115.
Meets a listed high-risk criterion based on lymph nodes, receptor status, or residual disease after treatment.
Completed primary therapy at least 4 weeks before study entry, with side effects resolved or improving.
Bone marrow test shows detectable disseminated tumor cells.
Age 18 or older with ECOG performance status of 2 or less.
not_for: Enrolled in another investigational therapy or trial within 30 days or 5 half-lives.
Prior abemaciclib, or a CDK4/6 inhibitor stopped less than 6 months before screening.
Known hypersensitivity to hydroxychloroquine or its derivatives.
Currently taking tamoxifen, or major surgery within 14 days before randomization.
Pregnant or breastfeeding, or of reproductive potential without effective birth control.
